result.title: Should We Pay This Much for Robustness? Efficient Proxy Certificates with Marginal Guarantees
result.summary: Modern classifiers remain sensitive to small input perturbations, while strong model-agnostic robustness certificates such as randomized smoothing are often too expensive for deployment, requiring an extensive number (e.g. 2000) of model forward passes per input. We propose a framework that delegates certification to a cheap proxy function while statistically controlling its deviation from the original sound certificate. Given an exchangeable unlabeled calibration set, we tune the proxy via robust conformal risk control to guarantee a bounded marginal (rather than pointwise) false-approval rate: the probability, over future inputs, that the proxy accepts an input whose prediction is flipped due to perturbation. The resulting proxy certificate can be used either as a standalone marginal certificate or as a fallback mechanism that invokes the expensive certificate only when the proxy rejects. We provide both single-sample and sample-heavy calibration recipes. Empirically, as a standalone certificate our method reduces the test-time certification cost to a single model forward while retaining much of the certified performance of randomized smoothing at small radii, and as a fallback it recovers the certified ratio of randomized smoothing at a more modest speedup. This enables cheap yet effective robustness guarantees for larger architectures such as vision transformers and language models.

AI.brief_summary: 提出把鲁棒性认证交给廉价代理函数，并借助无标注校准集上的 robust conformal risk control 控制代理与原可靠证书的偏差，使误认证率在边际意义上受限；代理既可单独使用，也可作为回退机制，仅在代理拒绝时才调用昂贵的 randomized smoothing 认证，从而把测试期认证成本降到一次前向。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「廉价代理 + 统计风险控制 + 仅在拒绝时回退到昂贵验证」的结构，可能为 LVR 中低成本判断推理状态是否可信、以及何时触发额外计算或证据获取（LOOK/STOP 的成本权衡）提供概念与方法线索，但需核查从对抗鲁棒性认证迁移到多模态推理的可行性。
